failure_surface: Python JSON-Schema regex end-anchor behavior allows values outside the intended exact immutable-reference producer/parser language.

oracles.title: A schema-valid state-revision id can produce a canonical ref rejected by every Decision 006 lifecycle base field
source_facts: Python regex $ accepts a position immediately before one final LF.
_assert_canonical_subset permits NFC control characters such as LF inside strings.
make_immutable_ref percent-encodes non-unreserved UTF-8 bytes, so an LF in the logical id is represented canonically as %0A.
PR #15 lifecycle base patterns allow only raw [a-z0-9._-]* in the state-revision logical-id component and therefore reject %0A.
oracles.continuity_failure: The repaired lifecycle contracts do not accept every exact immutable reference currently producible from an object accepted by the current state-revision contract. A replacement occupant can therefore hold a canonical state revision that cannot be named as the exact base of the three lifecycle objects.
oracles.repair_requirement: Do not encode producer-language assumptions with Python-sensitive ^...$ regexes. Make id/reference validation use semantics that cannot admit a final LF by anchor convention, and add a regression proving every valid state-revision identity produced by the current validator can cross the Decision 006 lifecycle boundary.

oracles.title: A lifecycle exact-base string with a trailing LF is contract-valid but parser-invalid

observed_results.parse_immutable_ref: rejected because the digest component contains the trailing LF

oracles.continuity_failure: Schema acceptance is still wider than the canonical Stage 2 parser language despite ADV-026-A's percent-encoding repair.
oracles.repair_requirement: Use an exact end-of-string mechanism or parser-backed semantic validation so trailing line terminators cannot satisfy an exact immutable-reference field.
